To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose Meta GNN, which is a novel metagraph neural network architecture for semi supervised learning on attributed heterogeneous information networks.

(i) Meta GNN, our metagraph neural network, outperforms state of the art baselines by 6% MicroF1, and (ii) Meta GNN learns interpretable metagraph attention weights that are indicative of the relative importance of metagraph semantics in a semi supervised node classification task.
Meta GNN is an effective semi supervised node classification method for Attributed HETerogeneous Information Networks.

we propose a novel neural model for semi supervised learning in AHINs that leverages metagraph structured neighborhood aggregation to learn higher order semantics, and is able to capture the semantics of typed relationships between diverse types of nodes.

metagraphs provide a rich semantic abstraction to model higher order relationships, and can be leveraged for SSL on AHINs.
